summary: Build local-government crisis communication skills with CERC, ISO frameworks, message mapping, and practical response exercises. Enrol today.
lede: Crisis communication training helps local government communicators and emergency managers coordinate public information during fast-moving incidents. It develops practical skills in assessing risks, validating incident information, mapping key messages, and preparing holding statements and press briefings. Participants also practise coordinating stakeholders and media, responding to misinformation, publishing accessible digital updates, and reviewing communication performance after an incident.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who coordinate public information, emergency response communication, community updates, and executive briefings within local government. It suits intermediate practitioners who already handle routine communications and need a stronger operating model for high-pressure incidents.
prerequisites: You should have working experience in local-government communications, public information, emergency management, public health communication, community engagement, or service leadership. No coding or programming is required. Bring examples of existing communication procedures, templates, or anonymized incident materials if available.
